2004 was the year of the Canadians!

Friday's last chance qualifier had 90 players, with 13 new people
becoming qualified on the day. The final was over in less than 45
minutes with Remy Auclair of Quebec winning the event.

Saturday's North American Continental Championship ended up with 60+
players, exact numbers to be provided later. Christian Chenard won
with a modified version of his Toreador Antitribu Embrace/Palla Grande
deck from 2 years ago. Hughes Bertrand and Stephane Lavrut also made
it to the finals, to make it possible to have the last 30 minutes of
the event transpire only in French. They held off for the spectators,
and the game continued in English.

Congratulations to Remy and Christian!

Deck Name : Kamut Krisp
Author : Ankur Gupta

Crypt (12 vampires) Capacity min: 2 max: 8 average: 5.5
------------------------------------------------------------

3x Ingram Frizer 6 AUS OBF ani pot !Nosferatu:3
2x Teresita, The Godm 7 ANI OBF POT for !Nosferatu:3
2x Piotr Andreikov 2 aus Tzimisce:3
1x Tarbaby Jack 8 ANI OBF POT dom ser !Nosferatu:3
1x Kazimir Savostin 7 AUS VIC ani pot Tzimisce:3
1x Quira, The Bitch Q 6 AUS OBF obt tha !Malkavian:2
1x Colonel, The 5 AUS cel dem obf !Malkavian:3
1x Roger Farnsworth 4 OBF aus !Malkavian:3

Library (90 cards)
------------------------------------------------------------

Action (18)
9x Bloodwork
9x Reunion Kamut

Action Modifier (10)
4x Art of Memory, The
6x Cloak the Gathering

Action Modifier/Combat (7)
7x Swallowed by the Night

Ally (6)
6x Marijava Thuggee

Combat (8)
2x Aura Reading
1x Stunt Cycle
5x Thrown Sewer Lid

Event (1)
1x Unmasking, The

Master (15)
1x Admonitions, The
4x Blood Doll
3x Corporal Reservoir
1x Information Highway
1x Information Network
1x Kaymakli Nightmares
1x Nosferatu Kingdom
1x Remover
1x Watchtower: Four Ride Forth
1x Weeping Stone

Reaction (25)
6x Ministry
5x Spirit's Touch
6x Telepathic Misdirection
8x Wake with Evening's Freshness

Crafted with : Anarch Revolt Deck Builder.

[Begin Ankur's comments]

The deck name is from an unusually terrifying cereal of the same name. A version of this deck was in the Nosferatu Antitribu
newsletter from March 2004. Peter Bajika and I must share a brain, as he independently and simultaneously posted another very
similar version of this deck in the Nosferatu newsletter in the same month. (This is probably bad, since it means I'm vulnerable
to employing the Bajika Gambit. . . .) The deck is essentially a strong mix of intercept deterrent combat and bleeding at stealth.
The mid/end game is strongly affected by the presence of the Thuggees, who exist to torpor key minions with low blood (which will
be the case in the mid/end game). All of a sudden, the hit for three with the lid is extremely relevant for any deck without
prevention. The deck truly locks into high gear with a Sabbat prey. A Sabbat predator isn't bad either.

Here are some comments on deck construction:

Of the vampires in the crypt I least like Tarbaby Jack, as his special isn't of great use to me. I have considered doubling up (or
tripling up) on virtually every vampire in the crypt aside from Piotr and Ingram, but ultimately made no change in order to
minimize bad crypt draw. . . . . Probably the best choice to replace him is another Kazimir, though Mariano Pomposo and Soldat
aren't horrible choices either (but you lose the use of the Nosferatu Kingdom and the Information Network for these swaps).
Usually, everyone thinks Ingram is the best vampire in the crypt, but they just happen to all be wrong. Piotr consistently gains
about 16-20 pool for the deck before he bites it. He is the hoss of all that is good and holy, but not worth three copies. You may
notice that Peter and I share the same crypt. I originally had Korah in place of Quira, but once I saw his version of the deck, I
decided that Peter made good sense on the choice and switched.

I tried to make it an 80 card deck, but in most games, I do a good job of using most of the deck, so 90 cards seems to be the
lesser of two evils -- I'd rather flow cards slightly more poorly than not have cards to flow. (Though, incidentally, this logic
only works if you're decking yourself quite often.) Kaymakli Nightmares and Info Highway were included to handle a problem that I
often seemed to face with this deck: too much free pool in my uncontrolled region. I wanted to access that pool faster with these
cards. If I happen to draw an early Kaymakli (instead of the late draw I'm hoping for), it can really slow down other decks and
increases the value of the less enabled vampires in the crypt -- Piotr, Roger, and the Colonel.

Remover is the most golden card ever. It effectively serves as stealth for the Thuggees without using the precious little stealth
I have, as well as forcing my prey to use wakes. Weeping Stone was the best decision I made among the masters. Not sure about the
Nosferatu Kingdom, though it's probably solid math to keep it. I often have to fish to see my second Nosferatu Antitribu, but then
again, I fish quite often anyway. I guess it makes good use of the extra Ingrams. I'd like to fit in an extra Corporeal Reservoir
if possible. I considered Perfectionist, but this is a deck that not only doesn't necessarily need it, but really *really* doesn't
want it. I don't want to give anyone any incentive to block/deflect anything I do. It's critical that they take the small bleeds
and let the small bloat through. Momentum's Edge, on the other hand, *is* a card that would go quite well in this deck. Perhaps it
is the swap for Nosferatu Kingdom. Dunno, though, since if the deck has ousted, it's probably doing just fine, but if it's not,
you can still gain pool from Nosferatu Kingdom.

I have exactly one Stunt Cycle in the deck, primarily as anti-Ivory Bow tech. Never saw the dratted thing all day, and I really
really wanted it the final -- it would have saved me a trip to torpor. Probably not worth a second copy, though, as I'd rather
have dependable damage most of the time. Aura Reading saved my butt at both levels in many games.

Art of Memory is the best card in the whole freaking deck. I ousted several times only as a result of this card. It's stealth,
combat, or actions -- whatever you need most -- that you decide *after* you draw into your replacements and see how the attempted
action played out. Hell, you can even slap them on a bleed for one. They probably won't even attempt to block, because they figure
you have stealth in your hand that you'll just take back and use on the next action. An outstanding card. I toyed with adding
more, but they might be wasted slots. (Jamming on them is unlikely as you can cycle them on anything.) I basically want one in my
hand, and I pre-emptively use it before my hand turns into utter crap and needs to be flushed with Aura Reading/Admonitions.
Incidentally, the timing of getting back Admonitions around the table synchs up well with the Arts. I royally screwed up the use
of the Admonitions in the final, though. (Sorry Will!)

I struggled a lot with the choice of intercept. Six Ministries is usually about one too many, but I always want to have one in my
hand; six Misdirections irritates me, as I feel all sleazy and gooey when I bounce. But it's there nonetheless. Ideally, I'd
almost like another Spirit's Touch for the maneuver, but I can't imagine what I'd drop for it. Ministry isn't a good trade, since
any chump can use it (today, Chump = Teresita or Tarbaby), and is a whole lot of intercept at once. I forgot to swap out two Wakes
for two Forced Awakenings, which I think would have helped me out a couple of times.

Also, I really wanted more stealth in the deck for those situations when I'm bleeding a non-Sabbat prey. Adding another Cloak and
another Swallowed (or maybe two Swalloweds to also address the Spirit's Touch problem) would satisfy me, I think. Dunno what I
would/could drop for it. Maybe one Kamut for one Swallowed to start with, but then the deck would be less capable of bloating
mindlessly and being named after a cereal. ;)

Another interesting solution to my lack of stealth was suggested by R. Brian Smith and I think might just work if done well --
Derange your prey to make them Sabbat. I have enough Malk Antis in the crypt to support such an idea, and it's probably worth it
to slot in 2-3 Deranges in total. The trick is just to find a small enough target, since Derange only works on younger vampires.
(Ironically enough, this might justify swapping back to Korah.) Even if you can't use it on your immediate prey, if someone is
deranged down the line, it'll be good for you in the end. It has the side benefits of:
a) introducing a (D) action that might be directed at you to block,
b) either forcing them to have wakes or burning blood off of vampires (which give the Thuggees more tasty targets), and
c) eliminating dangerous votes from the table.

[End Ankur's comments]

Well I was nuked by the deck in one of the preliminary rounds
(not that it says much). I think it was Saturday and not Friday, but
I'm not certain. Christian was my predator.

Table:
!Malk Stealth bleed -> David Tatu (deck not easily described) ->
->Christian -> John (me) -> !Nos rush deck

I ended up with a VP for outsing the !nos, Christian got the other 4.

Deck starts with Jost (+1 stealth all actions)
Grabbing embraces is then a 2 stealth action
Consang boon is then a 2 stealth action.
He used the stealth ritus for three stealth with Jost
or two stealth with another.

The weenies did nothing but create other weenies.
All key actions were conducted by non embraces,
non-thin blooded seers.

Sunset strip meant all his vampires hunted at 2 stealth.
Foundation exhibit gave him all the votes he needed.

The table I was at had rabid !malks cross table from this deck,
bleeding Mr Tatu heavily (who was contesting The Beast cross table)
and it looked like David was going to fold quickly. Christian pretty much
stated he was going to bloat like a madman to survive the oncoming
!malks. (and he did bloat but the malks failed to come thru)

I liked the idea of a no pressure predator, knew I would pay for it later,
but hoped to pick up a VP or two before that happened.
So we let him pass a Consang Boon or two, and get a few more
weenies. The !Nos were popping the malks slowly, the malks were pressing
forward, David was walling up, Christian was bloating.

I ousted the !Nos with a Fame yo-yo and was close to ousting the !malks
but then Christian pulled off a three stealth dramatic upheaval to sit in
front of
the !malks. (it was more complicated than that, first he tried to oust
through
me after pentexing one of the malks, when he realized he could not do it in
a single
turn, he then removed the pentex, then drew into the Upheaval to move in
front of the
malks.) At this point Christian had something like 10+ minions and
a whole lotta pool. Simple attrition handed him the game. He ousted the
!malks, then
Mr Tatu, then myself.

For the record I was running second traditions with a smattering of
transient intercepts (able to reach 3/4 intercept on occasion) and
I did manage to catch Jost once or twice but being able to reliably
put down two to three stealth made reliable intercept difficult. And those
damned
change of Targets helped him escape a few more times.

Reasons he won IMO: (that game)
1. cross table !malks distracted the table from his threat and shut down his
predator.
2. Jost's stealth let him get his essential actions through more often than
not
3. Massive bloat

If I had gone backwards more could I have stopped him? Unsure. His deck
was rolling really nice and I had no idea he was running 40+ master cards
based on his card play.
To shut him down would have required everything I had and then some help
from others on top of it (my minions were large, not enough actions),
leaving my
predator to run a-muck at will.

In hindsight we probably should have let the !malks kill Mr. Tatu quicker
(by not
interfering with the !malks) so that we could match the stealth bleed
against massive
bloat. But that did not happened and we hamstrung the !malks before they
managed to oust Mr. Tatu.

I did not watch any of Christian's other games.

-JTP

My guess is: being weenie covers a LOT of holes in strategy.
Aside from the castration of The Embrace, the other reason I gave
up on it for the most part was in tournaments, you run into too
many people with copious amounts of intercept who will generally
spend it every time they see an Embrace. Since Embrace is
undirected, you frequently find yourself frustrated by whatever
your prey lets through, your predator won't. I never tried
Embrace/Obfuscate, Embrace/Protean, or Embrace/Obtenebration
strategies which in retrospect, would have worked better than
the stuff I came up with.

Anyway, be that as it may, this deck seems to cover the same
issue using Creepshow Casino (I tried this as well - helps, but
by itself doesn't fix the problem), Stealth Ritus, and Jost
Werner's inherent stealth. The Embraces lose their discipline
card but the use of Palla Grande makes them 2 bleeders, which is
*much* more effective when you choose to go over the top. The
use of Foundation Exhibit makes them all voters, at least for
a turn. For situations where merely having lots of vampires
of (for instance) a given clan, The Embrace is still a useful card.

Without trying to build or use this deck, I make the following
comments, which I admit may miss some details about it for lack
of study:

* Dunno why he's using so many Thin-Blooded Seers. They're
cheaper but clanless and thus would not appear to ever be 2-bleeders
or voters. I suppose the one advantage is that an Embrace can
create a TBS but not another Embrace.

Hey Peter,

> Yeah, I'm kind of in the dark as to how the deck works. I mean, clearly, it
> does. But it looks like it has an awful lot of holes in it that are the
> types of holes that are exploited by many tournament strategies.

That's funny - when I looked at the deck, I thought to myself, "Wow,
it has very few holes and not much can defend against it."

I hope that Christian will comment himself. Here are my thoughts:

> But it doesn't have much stealth

Huh? It has *permanent* stealth! All the vamps are hunting at +2
stealth, and that's the main blood gain. A 1-cap hunting at +2
stealth will generally go unblocked IMO, especially when you take that
action 5 times per turn, and Jost hasn't acted yet. Jost and Jessica
vote at +4 stealth with Creepshow and the Ritus. I think this deck
does a great job of taking advantage of permanents.

Also, since hunting is the main pool gain, you can use Heidelberg and
the Communal Haven to swap blood around as necessary. Let the weenies
hunt, and Jost can call those important votes or make more babies.

A deck that has lots of untaps AND a minion with permanent intercept
AND permanent combat could hurt this deck a lot, but then there's
always Pentex.

> it doesn't have much combat defense (so Rush decks might eat it),

Rush decks are somewhat rare in tournaments, and torporing a 1-cap
minion per rush isn't so horrendous.

With Hungry Coyote, Life in the City, Giant's Blood, Hunting Ground,
Coven, Jake Washington, Heidelberg, and Communal Haven, this deck has
fast recovery if minions do go to torpor.

> it doesn't have much bleed defense (same with S+B)

It has fine bleed defense! The defense is: gain more pool than
anyone can possibly bleed. The Tributes, the Con Boons, Art Scams,
and the low minion cost will keep this deck alive.

Also, if your predator is a bleed deck, there's a decent chance it
doesn't have +2 intercept for multiple actions, and in that case the
table will be likely to support your bloat actions.

> it has a lot of masters that likely get jammed in your hand.

Parthenon and Dreams help. 7 trifles. A good number of those
masters can be safely discarded at the end of your turn once you
already have the permanent in play. Also, you don't need many
non-master cards in your hand for this deck to work; generally you
just hunt or bleed, maybe Jost calls 1 vote or makes a baby.

> So maybe I'm missing a vital part of the strategy?

Another really strong thing about this deck is that it can build up
fairly inconspicuously, better than other weenie decks. You don't
have 4 minions on the 2nd turn, with people screaming "KILL THE
WEENIES!" It's a slightly slower process that's less offensive than
standard weenies. Also, people must try a lot harder to mess with
you, even if they want to; permanent stealth is solid!

Most of the time you'll just be hunting and taking pool gaining
actions; the table generally doesn't care too much about that, and
instead only your predator will hate it (but what else is new?) Then,
when you're ready, this deck is very effective at lunging and being
unstoppable.

It will be difficult for the table to gang up on you at the right
moment - too soon and your predator has an easy win; too late and
you're unstoppable. From my experience, it's unlikely that the table
will turn against you if the vast majority of your actions are hunting
and pool gain. Making babies may cause some hate, but even then
you're not going forward very hard, until it's time to lunge.

Finally, a lot of the power of this deck comes from the Master cards,
and people generally don't have much defense against Master cards -
i.e. Sudden Reversal. For all the important Masters, this deck has
multiple copies even if one or two do get Suddened.

I would love to build this deck and play it, but it has... 49 rares!

I wonder if Anthelios would be good in this deck? Hmm. Now that I
think about it, this deck's biggest weaknesses are weenie hosers like
Snipe Hunt (who plays with that?), Aranthebes (Jost can still get rid
of it, and you can still bleed for 1 with Palla Grande), and one
really deadly card: Nightmares Upon Nightmares.

My $0.02,

Ira

Messages.Author: Christian Chenard
Messages.Body:
> Congratulations to Remy and Christian!

Thanks a lot. I'm happy I won.

I've read everything posted on the thread so far. Fine arguments
coming from all sides. Here's what I have to say (warning: long
post!).

About my deck:
(keeping in mind that there's always two sides to a coin)

The goods:

- It can gets lots of minions out
- It can generate lots of pool
- It can easily get vote lock to pass referendums
- It can bleed lots and oust in one turn
- It can generate some decent "permanent" stealth

The bads:

- It's minions are weak and pretty vulnerable in combat
- It doesn't have the blocking capacity that you usually expect from a
deck
- It's vote lock is only assured on it's own turn
- The "oust turn" must be prepared
- Intercept and rush do exist. The presence of large quantity of
either
- Like many deck, it probably won't survive an early 4 on 1 gang up.
(if there was such a survivor deck everybody would be playing it)

Regarding comments made:

- Yes the deck works, for the reasons that others stated so I won't
repeat.

- Yes, there's a lot of master but considering the Triffles and the
fact that you can play 1 master a turn and discard 1, it's not a real
problem. The deck works based on "table permanents" not "hand
potential". I never felt "master jammed" even when I held 7 masters in
my hand (it happened during the NAC Final).

- Yes, the deck needs to build a little before it gets going. But it
starts building on turn 2 (or 3 at worst) and is usually quite set on
turn 4-5. That's better than most decks.

- Yes, multirush or wall deck can stop my deck. The problem is that
they'll have to commit most or all of their resource trying to stop my
deck while some deck other than theirs is making the gamewin. Odds are
that at one point they'll cut me some slack to focus on the new
menace, when that time comes I just start rebuilding.

-Thin Blooded Seer are there for "historical" reason. In my old
version of the deck, Embraces at 2 cap (with presence and free
Majesty) generated other Embraces in an exponantial way with Hungry
Coyote. When all the CE erratas kicked in I was bummed because my best
deck had died. Thin Blooded Seer gave a second chance to the "weenie
breeding" strategy and I just had to give it a try. I admit Thin
Blooded Seer is not as great an action at 0 stealth but my prey will
usually let it go saving it's blockers for potential bleeds while my
predator will want to block his own pred most of the time. Looking
back on it, I would probably remove some of the TBS to include other
useful things.

About the NAC metagame:

I know my logic on this is quite linear. I know it's not the whole
thruth but I still think it's mostly true. This thinking was forged by
my prior Gencon experiences and led me to play that deck.

People go to the NAC to try to win it. To get to the finals, at least
2 solid wins in prelims are needed. It's a "make it big or break it
big" environment and you can afford one slip. This means you need to
have a deck that goes forward with a potential to quickly oust more
than 1 person (before the VPs start splitting on the table). I think
my deck meets this criteria.

My weaknesses are combat and intercept but rush decks (combat) are
slow if they ever do oust many people while wall decks (intercept)
usually don't get much more than 2 VPs in a 2 hour game. This means I
don't expect to encounter to many of those types of deck at the NAC
because people who make winning a priority won't play them (remember
that people go to the NAC to try to win it). So even if I do meet a
wall or rush deck, there is still a 50% chance that it is sitting
cross-table from you (in a 5 player game). So to end up sitting at a
position known as the "dead seat" for my deck at the NAC is unlikely.
If it happens (and it did in round 3) it represents the one mistake
I'm allowed.

My super brief analysis of the final:

I was lucky to have the rush deck sitting cross-table, to have my prey
and grand prey play the same crypt while my predator made himself
public enemy #1 before I could.

Some people say I played a great game. I just say I played the cards
as they came out of the deck. True, I did decide to put those cards
there in the first place and didn't make any major mistake. Still, you
could say I was lucky to win the NAC and be right. I don't mind, I'm
just excited that I'm going to get my face on a card...

Well here you have it folks. The comments of the winner. Hope I didn't
bore you too much.
